subject: physics
title: Newton's third law
key_idea: Whenever two objects interact, the forces they exert on each other are equal in size, opposite in direction and the same type. The two forces act on different objects, so they never cancel each other out.

blocks.text: Newton's third law is about pairs of forces. Whenever two objects interact, the forces they exert on each other are equal and opposite.

items: If object A pushes on object B, then B pushes back on A.
The two forces are the **same size** and act in **opposite directions**.
They are the same type of force, such as two contact forces.
They act at the same time.

items.meaning: The two forces two objects exert on each other.
A situation where the forces on an object are balanced.

blocks.text: The forces act on different objects

items: One force acts on object A. The other acts on object B.
They never act on the same object, so they cannot cancel each other out.
Two forces on one object are not an interaction pair, even if they are equal and opposite.

diagram.alt: Sort pairs of forces into Newton's third law pairs and pairs that are not.
diagram.prompt: Is each pair of forces a Newton's third law interaction pair?

items.text: Force of the mug on the table, and force of the table on the mug
Force of the water on the rocket, and force of the rocket on the water
Force of the racket on the ball, and force of the ball on the racket
Weight of the mug, and the force of the table on the mug
Driving force and air resistance on a car at a steady speed
Forward force and resistive force on a swimmer

items: Forces in an interaction pair are equal in size and opposite in direction.
The two forces act on different objects.
Name both objects: the force of A on B, and the force of B on A.

blocks.text: The law applies to objects at rest and to objects that collide or accelerate.

items: A mug on a table: the mug pushes down on the table, and the table pushes up on the mug.
A rocket: the rocket pushes water down, and the water pushes the rocket up.
A racket and ball: the force on the ball is equal and opposite to the force on the racket.
Two skaters: if A pushes B with 30 N, B pushes A with 30 N in the opposite direction.

blocks.text: The forces on the two objects are equal, but the accelerations are not equal if the masses differ. Apply Newton's second law to each object separately.

blocks.label: Newton's second law
where: F: resultant force in newtons, N
a: acceleration in metres per second squared, m/s²

items: Use the law for rockets, engines and collisions: the thing pushed pushes back.
Equal forces do not mean equal accelerations when the masses differ.
Check every answer says which object each force acts on.

checks.a: When two objects interact, the forces they exert on each other are equal and opposite.

checks.q: A mug rests on a table. Name the two forces in the interaction pair.
checks.a: The force of the mug on the table and the force of the table on the mug.

checks.q: Skater A pushes skater B with a force of 30 N. What force does A feel from B?

worked_example.question:
Air is taken into the front of an aircraft engine and pushed out of the back of the engine.

Explain the effect this has on the engine.
answer_points: The engine pushes the air backwards, so there is an (equal) force from the air on the engine
This force pushes on the engine and aircraft in the opposite direction, forwards
worked_example.tip: The second mark only scores if the first has been scored. If neither is scored, 'pushes the engine forwards' earns 1 mark.

worked_example.question:
A tennis ball is travelling towards a racket at a velocity of 8.2 m/s.
The ball is hit back in the opposite direction at a velocity of 15 m/s.
The ball has a mass of 0.075 kg.
The ball is in contact with the racket for 12 ms.

Describe how Newton's Third Law of Motion applies to the collision between the racket and the ball.
answer_points: The forces are equal (the same size)
The forces are opposite in direction
The forces act on different bodies: one acts on the racket, one acts on the ball
They are the same type of force, both contact forces
worked_example.tip: Any two points score the 2 marks. No marks for answers in terms of energy.

blocks.text: In a collision, the force on each object is equal and opposite and lasts for the same time. So the changes in momentum are equal and opposite.

blocks.label: Force and change in momentum
where: v: final velocity in metres per second, m/s
u: initial velocity in metres per second, m/s
t: time of the collision in seconds, s

items: Force is linked to change in momentum, by Newton's second law (the equation above).
The time of the collision is the same for both objects.
So the momentum change is the same size for both, in opposite directions.
Total momentum before equals total momentum after, if no external forces act.

worked_example.question:
A water rocket lifts off the ground when water is pushed out of the bottom of the rocket.

Explain how Newton's third law applies to the rocket as it lifts off the ground.

Use ideas about the force of the water and the force of the rocket.
answer_points: The water pushes on the rocket and the rocket pushes on the water
The forces act in opposite directions
The forces are the same size (and type)
Each force acts on a different object
worked_example.tip: Any two of the four points. 'Forces are equal and opposite' alone earns 2 marks.
